title: Legislative districts of Sultan Kudarat
wikitext:
{{Politics of the Philippines}} [[File:Districts of Sultan Kudarat.jpg|thumb|Map of 1st and 2nd Legislative Districts of Sultan Kudarat]] The '''legislative districts of Sultan Kudarat''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Sultan Kudarat]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Cotabato}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Sultan Kudarat were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935) and [[Cotabato]] (1935–1972). The enactment of Presidential Decree No. 341 on November 22, 1973 created the Province of [[Sultan Kudarat]] out of the reduced [[Cotabato]] Province's southern municipalities.{{cite web|title=Presidential Decree No. 341 - Creating the Provinces of North Cotabato, Maguindanao and Sultan Kudarat|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1973/11/22/presidential-decree-no-341-s-1973/|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|last=Marcos|first=Ferdinand E.|access-date=November 19, 2017|date=November 22, 1973}} This new province was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region XII]] from 1978 to 1984. Sultan Kudarat first gained separate representation in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]], when it returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province constituted a [[#Lone District (defunct)|lone congressional district]],{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance |website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} and elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The approval of Republic Act No. 9357 on October 10, 2006 increased Sultan Kudarat's representation by reapportioning the province into two congressional districts,{{cite web|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2006/ra_9357_2006.html|title=Republic Act No. 9357 - An Act Reapportioning the Province of Sultan Kudarat into Two Legislative Districts|website=The LawPhil Project|date=October 10, 2006|access-date=November 23, 2017|author=Congress of the Philippines}} which elected their separate representatives starting in the [[2007 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2007 elections]]. == 1st District == *'''[[Cities of the Philippines|City]]''': [[Tacurong]] *'''[[Municipalities of the Philippines|Municipalities]]''': [[Columbio, Sultan Kudarat|Columbio]], [[Isulan, Sultan Kudarat|Isulan]], [[Lambayong, Sultan Kudarat|Lambayong]], [[Lutayan, Sultan Kudarat|Lutayan]], [[President Quirino, Sultan Kudarat|President Quirino]] *'''Population (2020)''': 427,963{{cite web|url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx|website=Philippine Statistics Authority|date=2015|title=Population of Population of Legislative Districts by Region, Province, and Selected Highly Urbanized/Component City: 2015|access-date=November 18, 2017}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
